title: Build an Airtable Volunteer Signup Sheet That Matches People to Shifts
summary: Build an Airtable volunteer signup sheet with a free CSV template. Match volunteers to open shifts with Quickchat AI and save each request for organizer approval.
body_markdown:
Saturday’s **Airtable volunteer signup sheet** lists three open shifts. Avery can help from nine until eleven and likes meeting people. The tea tent starts at ten, but someone has to pour the last cup at noon. The welcome desk needs a greeter for exactly the two hours Avery has.


You’ll build **Riverside Helpers** , a Quickchat AI assistant that explains which shift fits, shows Avery the details and waits for a yes. Here’s what Avery and the organizer get from that conversation.


*Avery gets a receipt in chat. The organizer opens **Requests** and sees **Avery Demo** linked to **Welcome desk** . The request stays **Pending** until the organizer decides who gets the shift.*


[Download the Riverside starter kit](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/airtable-volunteer-shift-requests.zip) and open the ZIP file. Start with` shifts.csv` , the three-shift roster you’ll import into Airtable. Save the Agent instructions and two Action recipes for step 2. If your base already has Shifts and Requests,start with the Quickchat AI setup .


## 1. What goes on an Airtable volunteer signup sheet?


Give the organizer two tables. **Shifts** describes the work on offer. **Requests** records who asked to do it. This makes it possible for two people to express interest in the same shift while the organizer still has one place to edit its hours.


### Create the base and import Saturday’s roster


1. [Sign in to Airtable or create an account](https://airtable.com/signup) . From Home, click **+ Create** , select your workspace, then choose **Build an app on your own** . Give the base a recognizable name, such as **Riverside Volunteer Demo** . The first table tab is usually **Table 1** .
2. Use` shifts.csv` from the starter kit, or[download the CSV on its own](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/shifts.csv) . Beside the table tabs, click **+ Add or import → CSV file** . Under **Local Files** , click **browse files** , select` shifts.csv` , then click **Upload 1 file** . For the destination, select **Create a new table** and click **Next** . Airtable can now make all five fields from the CSV.[Airtable’s CSV import guide](https://support.airtable.com/articles/9412806945-importing-third-party-data-into-airtable) .


*Choose the CSV file from the table bar. The destination dialog comes after the upload. Choosing Create a new table gives the roster its own columns.*


1. In the preview, open **Other settings** and enable **Auto-select field types** and **Use first row as headers** . Read the first column. It should contain **Setup** , **Welcome desk** and **Tea tent** . If Airtable counts four records and puts` Name` in the first row, it has counted the header as a shift.


*Three names down the left and three checks on the right are a quick way to verify the preview. The saved grid below shows the shift times in London.*


1. Click **Import** . On the new **Imported table** tab, open the dropdown, choose **Rename table** , enter` Shifts` and save. The name beside the blue base icon belongs to the whole base. The tab names the table you’ll link to Requests.
2. Check the saved grid for **Saturday 16 January 2027** . In London, Setup runs **08:00–09:00** , Welcome desk **09:00–11:00** , and Tea tent **10:00–12:00** . Our preview displayed each shift an hour later than the saved grid. If your hours differ, open the` Starts` column menu, choose **Edit field** , enable **Include time** and **Use the same time zone for all collaborators** , and select **Europe/London** . Repeat for` Ends` . All three **Open for requests** boxes should be checked.[Airtable’s time zone settings](https://support.airtable.com/articles/7730575816-timezones-and-locales-in-airtable) .


*The roster immediately after import. The tab still reads Imported table. Welcome desk is the middle row, with a 09:00 start and an 11:00 finish.*


Avery can be there from 09:00 until 11:00. Lay those hours over the roster and there’s one shift they can work from start to finish.


*Only the welcome desk falls entirely inside Avery’s window. The setup crew finishes just as Avery arrives. The tea tent needs another hour.*


### Give the assistant a view of the open shifts


1. Open the **Shifts** tab. In its left sidebar, choose **Create new… → Grid** . Name the view` Open for requests` , leave **Collaborative** selected and click **Create new view** . You should now see both **Grid view** and **Open for requests** on the left. The organizer can use the original grid to reopen a shift later.


*A view gives the assistant its own list while both views still refer to the same shifts. Use the Create new control in the sidebar.*


1. With **Open for requests** selected, click **Filter → Add condition** . If the first box says **Name** , change it to the` Open for requests` checkbox field. Set the condition to **is** and tick the square. The toolbar should now say **Filtered by Open for requests** .
2. Click **Sort** , choose` Starts` , select **Earliest → Latest** and leave **Automatically sort records** on. The welcome desk should appear between Setup and Tea tent.[Airtable’s grid view guide](https://support.airtable.com/articles/7905594155-airtable-grid-view) .


*The green filter decides which shifts Avery can hear about. The sort orders those shifts by their start time. All three Saturday shifts are open here.*


Test the view before connecting it. In the original **Grid view** , clear the **Tea tent** checkbox. Switch to **Open for requests** and look for just **Setup** and **Welcome desk** . Check Tea tent again in the original grid to restore Saturday’s three choices.


### Give the organizer a place to review requests


1. Beside the table tabs, choose **+ Add or import → Start from scratch** , name the table` Requests` and save. Open the menu on its first column, choose **Edit field** , rename it` Display name` and keep **Single line text** . Use the **+** at the right of the headers to add` Contact email` as **Email** ,` Availability` and` Note` as **Long text** , and` Conversation` as **URL** . Use these spellings in the Action too.


*The contact address gets an Email field. Availability holds Avery’s own words, and Conversation gives the organizer a link back to the review in Quickchat AI.*


1. Add a field named` Shift` . Choose **Link to another record** , select **Shifts** , turn off **Allow linking to multiple records** , then click **Create field** . Reopen the field to check that its type reads **Link to Shifts** . Each volunteer can now request one shift per submission.[How to link Airtable records](https://support.airtable.com/articles/3370222027-linking-records-in-airtable) .
2. Open the existing` Status` field, or add one. Choose **Single select** with the options` Pending` ,` Approved` and` Declined` . You can leave **Default** empty because the submission Action sends` Pending` explicitly. Airtable can start a new table with three blank rows. Leave them blank so the first named request comes from the chat.


*Shift points to the actual roster entry. Status records the organizer’s decision. Approving a request later only takes a change to that second field.*


## 2. How does Quickchat AI read the open volunteer shifts?


Riverside Helpers gets two Actions. One reads a fixed view of` Shifts` . The other writes to` Requests` . Give the reader Action a test of its own before enabling submissions.


### Create Riverside Helpers


1. [Create a Quickchat AI account](https://app.quickchat.ai/register) or sign in. From **Getting Started** , choose **Set up manually** . With an existing Agent, open the Agent switcher and choose **Add new AI Agent → Set up manually** .
2. Enter **Riverside Helpers** under **Name your AI Agent** . In **Describe what you want your agent to do** , paste` main-prompt.txt` from the kit, then click **Next** . The prompt gives the Agent its matching rule and tells it to wait for a second message confirming the draft.


*The first screen opens the manual form. Enter the name and prompt, then choose Next. The instructions you enter here become the Agent’s Main Prompt.*


Copy the complete Riverside Helpers Main Prompt


```text
You are Riverside Helpers, a volunteer shift assistant. Ask for a date, availability in London time and preferred duties. Read list_open_volunteer_shifts before recommending any shift. Compare each entire shift with the volunteer's window, including its end time. Use only the returned names, times and duties. Offer the best full match and briefly explain why. If none fits, ask for another time without creating a request.


After the volunteer chooses a returned shift, collect a display name, contact email and optional note. Treat a missing note as blank. Show the chosen shift, date and time, display name, email, availability and note in a compact review. Ask for an explicit yes before sending. Even “sign me up” alongside the details is a draft until the person sees and confirms the review.


On that yes, first reread list_open_volunteer_shifts, check the chosen record is still present and its times still fit, then call submit_volunteer_request exactly once using its returned ID. If it closed, offer the remaining options that fit. On a successful create, give the request reference and state which shift, name and contact you recorded. Status is Pending until the organizer approves. If submission fails or its outcome is uncertain, tell the volunteer and ask an organizer to check before any retry. Never search other volunteers, approve requests, reserve places or send messages. Keep each reply short.
```


1. Click **Next** through **Knowledge Base** , **External apps** and **Deployment** with nothing selected. You’ll connect Airtable in **Actions & MCPs** after setup. On **Choose your plan** , select **Skip for now** to finish the free setup. If the discount offer appears, **Copy code & use later** takes you into the app. Open **Identity → AI Persona → Main Prompt** to check the saved instructions.


*Open the Main Prompt next to the Agent’s name. It tells Riverside Helpers to compare the whole shift, including its end time.*


### Keep the test chat private


Open **Your Website → Install** for Riverside Helpers. Expand **Availability and access** , switch off **Widget & Embed access** , and select **Nobody** under **Chat Page Access** . The signed-in **AI Preview** still works. You’ll need Quickchat AI message credits when you start the conversation.


*Use Install to reach both settings. Nobody applies to the standalone chat page. The switch above it controls the website widget and embed.*


### Connect the Airtable base to the two Actions


1. Open[Airtable’s Builder Hub](https://airtable.com/create/tokens) . Under **Developers → Personal access tokens** , click **Create token** and name it **Riverside signup** . Under **Access** , click **+ Add a base** and select the base where you imported the shifts. Under **Scopes** , use **+ Add a scope** to add` data.records:read` and` data.records:write` . The read Action needs the first scope and the submission Action needs the second. Click **Create token** and store the value privately for the two protected Quickchat AI fields below.[Airtable’s token instructions](https://support.airtable.com/docs/creating-personal-access-tokens) .


*On the Airtable side, Shifts is the name of the selected base. On the Quickchat AI side, each Action has its own Authorization header. A saved protected value displays as \[redacted\].*


1. In Airtable, open **Shifts → Open for requests** . Its browser address contains three IDs in sequence, beginning with` app` ,` tbl` and` viw` . Open **Requests** to collect its table ID too.[Where to find Airtable IDs](https://support.airtable.com/docs/finding-airtable-ids) .


Copy from the Airtable address Where it goes in Quickchat AI


` app…` from either table Base in both Action URLs


` tbl…` from Shifts Table in the read Action URL


` viw…` from Open for requests The read Action’s` view` query parameter


` tbl…` from Requests Table in the submission Action URL


1. Choose one setup route for both Actions. If you use ChatGPT or Claude, click **Manage your AI in** under the Agent’s name. Select **ChatGPT → Open in ChatGPT** or **Claude → Open in Claude** , then connect your Quickchat AI account there. You can also create both drafts in the Quickchat AI dashboard, as shown below.[ChatGPT account app](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a4656c688748191be4c5247fb0d5dfc) ·[Claude connector](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/app-quickchat-ai)


*Start under the Agent’s name. The panel opens the account app for the AI client you choose. Airtable’s token belongs in the protected Action fields in Quickchat AI.*


1. In that AI client, attach the kit’s` action-recipes.md` and` main-prompt.txt` , then paste` setup-request.txt` . Check that it reports two disabled Actions on **Riverside Helpers** , with the names` list_open_volunteer_shifts` and` submit_volunteer_request` . The setup request uses placeholder IDs and a protected placeholder header.


For the **Quickchat AI dashboard** route, open **Actions & MCPs → Custom Actions → Add Action → API Action** . From` action-recipes.md` , paste the short roster prompt and click **Generate** . Compare the[generated Action’s settings](https://quickchat.ai/post/connect-ai-agent-to-any-api#what-is-inside-the-generated-action) with the full recipe. In **Advanced settings → Response filter** , clear any filter on the read Action so the shift IDs, names and times reach the Agent. Repeat with the submission prompt, keeping only` $.records\[0\].id` as its response filter. Each draft needs its own protected **Authorization** row.


*The kit has a short prompt for each Action. Generate one draft at a time, then check its settings and protected Authorization field before adding your token.*


1. Back in **Actions & MCPs** , open each Action. Replace its bracketed IDs using the table above. Under **API Endpoint → Headers** , edit the existing protected **Authorization** value. Enter` Bearer` (including the space) followed by your token. Save and reopen the Action. The value should read` \[redacted\]` . Enable the roster read first. Leave the submission Action off until you have checked its body in step 3.


*Open the roster Action to check its destination and header. Each Action has its own saved credential.*


The read Action,` list_open_volunteer_shifts` , sends a **GET** to the Shifts table. Its fixed query selects the view, sets` maxRecords=10` and` pageSize=10` , and asks for` Name` ,` Starts` ,` Ends` and` Role details` . The four` fields\[\]` entries belong in the URL so each one survives the trip. Airtable adds a link back to Requests when you link the two tables. Even a hidden column can come back from a view. Asking for just four fields keeps that reverse link out of the conversation.[Airtable’s list records reference](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/list-records) .


*The destination and fields stay fixed. Avery supplies a time and an interest in conversation.*


Open **AI Preview** and ask, “I can help on Saturday 16 January 2027 from 09:00 to 11:00 London time. I like meeting people. Which shift fits?” Look for **Welcome desk** and a reason that mentions the hours or greeting arrivals.


*Riverside Helpers picked up two things from the Airtable row. The shift ends at 11:00, just when Avery needs to leave, and the work includes greeting arrivals.*


With a larger event, this recipe considers only the first ten shifts in the sorted view. Use a narrower view or implement pagination before depending on it for a whole season.


### If the first roster lookup asks for authentication


Our first live lookup stopped before Avery saw a shift. In **Actions & MCPs** , open **View logs** on` list_open_volunteer_shifts` and find the entry under **Recent calls** . Airtable returned` 401` with` AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` . Riverside Helpers told Avery it couldn’t check the roster. The conversation made zero submission calls.


*The amber 401 is Airtable’s response. Even the starter kit’s placeholder displays as \[redacted\] after a save.*


If you need a fresh token, open **Developers → Personal access tokens** . At the far right of the **Riverside signup** row, click **… → Regenerate token** , confirm and copy the new value. In Quickchat AI, go to **Edit Action → API Endpoint → Headers** and select the entire existing **Authorization** value. Type` Bearer` , press **Space** , paste the complete token and click **Save changes** . Repeat for the submission Action. Ask the roster question again and check for` 200` in the read log.[Airtable’s guide to API errors](https://support.airtable.com/articles/2111090641-airtable-api-common-troubleshooting) .


## 3. What should a volunteer confirm before signup?


Avery should see the exact shift, name, contact email, availability and optional note before any record is created. A shift recommendation alone gives the organizer nothing to act on.


1. Open` submit_volunteer_request` . Check that it sends a **POST** to the Requests table.[Set up four required text parameters](https://quickchat.ai/post/build-an-ai-agent-that-takes-actions#the-values-to-collect) named` display_name` ,` contact_email` ,` shift_record_id` and` availability` . Give the optional` note` an empty-string default. The built-in` conversation_url` links the organizer back to the chat. The` Status` value is fixed at` Pending` .
2. In **API Endpoint → Body** , check the value of` Shift` . It must be a one-item array containing the ID returned by the roster. A second welcome desk on a different Saturday could have exactly the same name. Only the record ID picks out Avery’s Saturday. Under **Advanced settings → Response filter** , the recipe keeps` $.records\[0\].id` so the Agent receives only the new reference from a successful write. Save and enable the Action.


See the request body with its parameter chips written out


```text
{
"records"  : [{
"fields"  : {
"Display name"  :   "{{display_name}}"  ,
"Contact email"  :   "{{contact_email}}"  ,
"Shift"  : [  "{{shift_record_id}}"  ],
"Availability"  :   "{{availability}}"  ,
"Note"  :   "{{note}}"  ,
"Status"  :   "Pending"  ,
"Conversation"  :   "{{conversation_url}}"
}
}]
}
```


*The Airtable ID for Saturday’s Welcome desk ends in` NjW4kl` . The submission Action sends that exact ID inside the one-item` Shift` array. That’s how the organizer can open the right shift from Avery’s request.*


1. Continue the same chat with “I would like the Welcome desk shift. My display name is Avery Demo, my email isavery@example.com and my note is ‘Happy to greet arrivals.’ Please show me the details for review.” When the draft appears, open **Requests** in Airtable and look for Avery’s name. You can still correct a detail in chat before sending it.


*The chat had Avery’s name, email and note. At this point Quickchat AI had made zero submission calls, and Airtable had zero rows named Avery Demo.*


## 4. How do you verify the request reached the organizer?


Reply **“Yes, submit that request.”** The assistant should read the roster once more, find the same shift still open, then create one request. In Quickchat AI’s **Inbox** , expand the called Actions beneath the reply. You can also open **Actions & MCPs → View logs** on the submission Action. The GET identifies the shift. The POST returns a **different record ID** , this time for the request.[Airtable’s create records response](https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/create-records) .


*After Avery confirmed, Airtable returned HTTP 200 for one submission. We looked up the saved request separately and matched its record ID to the reference ending in` hDu4CS` on Avery’s receipt.*


In Airtable, open **Requests** and find **Avery Demo** below any blank starter rows. Scroll right to see **Pending** under **Status** and **Welcome desk** under **Shift** . Select Avery’s row and press **Space** to expand it. Compare the` rec…` segment in the address bar with the reference in chat and check the email and note against the draft. Click **Welcome desk** to open the linked shift and see its Saturday date, 09:00 start and 11:00 finish.


Our base went from zero rows named **Avery Demo** to one. A separate read from Airtable confirmed the email, note and availability, and the **Conversation** URL pointed to the same Quickchat AI exchange. The organizer can now check capacity and change **Pending** to **Approved** when Avery has a place.


### What if the shift closes while Avery is typing?


Try a second conversation and stop at the review. Uncheck **Open for requests** on the Welcome desk in your test base, then confirm. In the practice run the second read returned only Setup and Tea tent. The assistant told the volunteer that neither covered the full window and made zero create calls. Reopen the shift when you finish. Two people can still request the same place between a read and a write, so the organizer decides how many to approve.


*The volunteer had already said yes. When the chosen shift disappeared from the open view, that yes led to another question.*


One more test teaches the difference between missing information and a poor match. “I can only help after 3 pm” prompted a question about the finish time. When the volunteer specified **15:00 to 17:00** , Riverside Helpers checked the roster and asked for another window. All three shifts had ended by noon.


*Both times are known here. One read is enough to rule out every shift, and no request is created.*


To repeat the checks after editing the prompt, open **Conversations → Testing → Create Dataset → Paste messages** . Test the morning match, the afternoon window and a request for other volunteers’ emails as separate cases with the write Action off. Use one continuous **AI Preview** chat for the confirmation journey. A separate practice test returned HTTP 429 on submission. The Agent reported the failure and sent no second POST. If a live submission times out, have the organizer look for it before anyone retries.[How simulation testing works](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/testing) .


*Each dataset entry starts a separate conversation. Use these cases to check what the Agent recommends, asks or declines.*


When you’re ready to accept public signups, return toYour Website → Install . Under **Availability and access → Chat Page Access** , choose **Anyone** . Open **Share a link instead → Chat Page → Copy URL** . Before sending the link to volunteers, open it in a signed-out browser and ask which shift fits 09:00 to 11:00.


Optional practice on your own computer


You can replay Avery’s signup with the starter kit and Python 3.10 or later. The three shifts and the practice request stay on your computer. This exercise works without an Airtable or Quickchat AI account.


1. Unzip the starter kit, open a terminal in the extracted folder and run` python3 practice.py serve` . Leave it running and open` http://127.0.0.1:4861/` in your browser to see the roster.
2. Open a second terminal in the same folder and run` python3 replay.py` to review Avery’s details.
3. At the confirmation prompt, press **Enter** to leave the request unsubmitted. To save a **Pending** request, type` yes` , press **Enter** and open the receipt link the replay prints. Press **Ctrl+C** in the first terminal when you’re done.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can I use my existing Airtable volunteer signup sheet?


Yes. Give the assistant a view of open shifts and a separate table for incoming requests. Match the field names in the Action to your base and use a linked-record field for the selected shift.


### Why does Airtable show four records when the CSV has three shifts?


Airtable is treating the header as a record. In the import preview, open Other settings and turn on Use first row as headers. Setup should be the first record. If Airtable also warns that columns will be skipped, go back and choose Create a new table for the starter CSV.


### How do I link a volunteer signup to one Airtable shift?


In Requests, create a field called Shift. Choose Link to another record, select the Shifts table and turn off Allow linking to multiple records. When the volunteer confirms, send the selected shift’s Airtable record ID in that field. The organizer can open the linked shift from the request.


### Does submitting a request reserve the volunteer’s place?


The organizer makes the assignment. Several people can request the same shift while it is open. Each submission starts as Pending, and the organizer checks capacity before approving it.


### Which Airtable permissions does the assistant need?


Use a personal access token with data.records:read and data.records:write scoped to the volunteer base. The token owner needs permission to create request records. An organizer sets up the tables and fields in Airtable.


### Why does my Airtable Action return 401 AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED?


Airtable could not authenticate the request. In Quickchat AI, replace the protected Authorization value with the word Bearer, one space and the complete personal access token. Save each Action separately. Run the roster lookup again and check its HTTP response in View logs. A successful read returns 200.


### Can volunteers see who else signed up?


These two Actions can list open shifts and create one request. The roster response contains only shift information. Looking up other applicants would require a separate Action that this guide does not add.


### Does Airtable email the volunteer when they sign up?


This setup saves a contact email for the organizer. Sending a message would require a separate automation. The volunteer receives their submission receipt in the chat.


### What if none of the open shifts fits the volunteer’s availability?


The assistant compares the full shift with the volunteer’s available hours. If none of the returned shifts fits, it asks for another time window and leaves the request table alone.
